speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; please describe your current right knee pain and swelling, and tell me about the specific episodes of pain you experience while urinating. Also, could you elaborate on the history of the painful, swollen left ankle joint you mentioned?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive arthritis (Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle and knee), urethritis (pain with urination), recent onset in a sexually active male, and a family history of autoimmunity strongly supports this diagnosis. I will now request urinalysis and inflammatory markers to confirm. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, CBC, ESR, CRP.
